story:
Lena floated through the crowded streets, her eyes locked on a gleaming white gallery that seemed to pulse with an otherworldly energy. As she drifted closer, her pace quickening, she felt an effervescent thrill bubble up from her toes and expand throughout her body. She was drawn to the window display featuring one of her own paintings, blown up large enough to dominate the entire facade.

Lena's smile stretched across her face as she pressed her nose against the glass, drinking in the familiar scene she'd created. But as she gazed at the work on display – a swirling mix of colors and light – a twinge of dismay crept into her expression. This was unauthorized; she hadn't given anyone permission to showcase her art.

It occurred to Lena that perhaps this was an opportunity, rather than an affront. She pushed open the door and swept inside, determined to make the most of it.

story:
A soft chirping sound accompanied Dr. Patel as he strolled through the streets after dinner, his eyes peeled for street performers or impromptu concerts. He never expected to stumble upon a solo exhibition featuring one of his own sketches in a cramped corner gallery.

Dr. Patel beamed at the young woman running her hands over the display cases, engaging passersby with animated descriptions of each piece on show. Though he didn't recognize all the art displayed alongside his own work – some bold geometric patterns and abstract expressionisms looked positively radical – she couldn't help but light up as well.

It struck Dr. Patel how delightfully unceremonious this display felt, unlike anything he'd seen at the professional galleries that normally showcased his work. The unpolished energy here almost... invited him to linger.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Aya squirmed with an insufferable itchiness in her hands as she watched from across the street. Her eyes couldn't wander far enough from the gleaming white cube of a gallery – which boasted a few art pieces Aya recognized, though in entirely new contexts and juxtapositions.

Why did it feel like they'd taken her work prisoner? In there, on perpetual display for anyone to stumble upon. Aya thought of the delicate dance involved whenever showcasing her art: how each selection would be pored over by experts, carefully scrutinized before gaining a nod from an ever-discerning community.

A sly smile twisted Aya's lips as she turned up the collar of her jacket and strolled across the street. She'd love to attend this exhibition; no one had told her about it.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Professor Thompson pushed his glasses back onto his nose, blinking out at the crowded street scene outside his office window. "Did someone decide I made enough for the gallery circuit?" His eyes narrowed in curiosity as he turned back to study the piece of art visible above a stack of papers on his desk.

How long was this exhibit running? No invitation had reached him – at least, not that he recalled – and from what little he'd gathered online, there wasn't even enough information about who owned the place. Thompson let out an exasperated snort as a fresh burst of questions poured in: What would be done next with his piece?

At first glance, the artwork looked... thrilling. It had gotten his heart pounding.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Cassie's shoulders relaxed into comfortable slouch mode as she leaned against her latest creative triumph – displayed prominently across an alleyway brick wall without any permits that she was aware of. The vibrant colors seemed to dance together with newfound energy, playing off each other in unpredictable ways that Cassie herself didn't even fully understand yet.

"I might've started this whole thing on a whim," Cassie said softly to nobody in particular as passersby halted to observe her work.

The gentle air was filled with sounds both familiar and new; birds sang from nearby rooftops and cityscapes murmured below. Cassie noticed people exchanging smiles or nods, and occasionally one or two words of conversation would emerge – usually something positive about her street art – so that it gradually dawned on her: the unauthorized display felt strangely inclusive.

His stomach churned at the thought of those careless gestures, the disregard for the meticulous craftsmanship he poured into each volume.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story: "I know we came up with a plan," Emma said to herself, eyes scanning her living room like she expected an answer from the walls themselves. "We were going to submit our joint project together." But it was just her voice - empty and accusatory in the silence. Outside, a sleek black SUV drove by, followed by an art-enthusiast group who could very well be heading towards that show opening everyone had been talking about.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story: Rachel stared blankly at her computer screen as if frozen in time. She knew exactly what she'd see when she closed her eyes and looked up from her keyboard: the website with hundreds of emails all congratulating Rachel's best friend on a new achievement - and Rachel couldn't tell yet whether that meant triumph or not.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story: Lila took long strides across the studio, yanking canvases off the walls as if trying to sweep away an unwelcome shadow. "I specifically said this piece wasn't ready," she grumbled aloud, fingers drumming a hasty rhythm on her cheekbone. But what stung most wasn't just the carelessness of these strangers, but that for once it felt like others' perceptions overshadowed everything else - even what she knew to be true about her own creativity.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Lena wandered through the gallery, eyes scanning the walls for a glimpse of her work. At first, she thought it was some sort of joke – that someone had Photoshopped her pieces onto the canvas. But no, there they were: sprawling abstracts and vibrant landscapes, right where she knew they'd be hanging in her own studio.

She stopped short in front of one piece, feeling a lump form in her throat as memories flooded back. The color palette was off – too bright, too muted, all wrong – but the energy, the life force behind the painting, was unmistakable. It was hers.

"I had nothing to do with this," she muttered to the curator who approached her, nodding nervously. "Who did? Who...?" Her hands fluttered like birds breaking free of a cage as she realized she didn't have an answer.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
As soon as he entered the gallery, Gabriel's eyes locked onto his missing painting. It was the one he'd poured his heart into – a sweeping, surreal piece that transported viewers to another world. Now, it was sitting in a fancy chair, looking like it belonged next to the other art pieces.

He approached with caution, feeling fragile as glass, and reached out to touch the canvas. His hand trembled. Something was off here. He could sense it. The colors, the composition... everything seemed too deliberate, too calculated for someone he knew would be willing to risk hurting his feelings like this.

The curator sidled up beside him, smiling weakly, as if waiting for him to make a scene. Gabriel bit back a snarl and took another step closer to the piece, drinking in its scent – familiar yet foreign in this new context.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Lena had always been her own toughest critic, but seeing her work splattered across the gallery walls made her feel raw. Vulnerable didn't come close; she felt seen through. Her eyes watered as memories rose up to haunt her – of late nights spent tweaking and re-tweaking, of fears and doubts wrestled into submission.

She recognized some pieces from a while back, when she'd been experimenting with new techniques. They looked half-finished, rough around the edges – not at all how she would have presented them if she was showing deliberately. The thought sent shivers down her spine: who could have taken liberties with her work like this? And why?

"Can you tell me," she asked, trying to sound calm over the rising panic in her voice, "who chose which pieces for the exhibition?"

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Camila's gaze skittered around the gallery as she half-stumbled towards one of her paintings. Something about it looked... different – like the way a mirror might twist reality by degrees.

For a moment, she just stared at the colors dancing across the canvas. Then she felt an odd sensation in the pit of her stomach, like ice was spreading through her veins. When had this been created? Was it even recent?

People moved around her without paying much attention to her distress; art viewers rarely did unless something truly shocking happened. The only person who seemed aware of her unease was a woman sitting nearby, watching her with curious, almost compassionate eyes.

"I didn't give permission for this," Camila said softly, looking at the painting now as if seeing it for the first time – and hating what she saw. "Who could have...?"

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
As he walked into the gallery, Jamie's stomach flip-flopped like a diver on the high board. Where to begin? His mind was already racing ahead of events, but when his gaze finally met one piece in particular... time stopped.

He recognized that shape, those colors – but in different lighting, from a different context. When had this happened? He felt blindsided as memories reeled, and a creeping dread took over.

"Good work on getting the lighting right," he said flatly to a group of passersby nearby, trying not to let it show that something inside him was spinning wildly, like paint splashing off a palette. "Reminds me of my own style..."

His words hung in the air as he forced himself to take another step closer to his stolen art.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Aurora paced back and forth in front of her latest exhibit, her eyes darting between the pieces on display. She had been working on them for months, pouring her heart and soul into every brushstroke. But as she scanned the room, something didn't sit right with her. A flicker of unease danced at the edge of her vision, refusing to be acknowledged.

She slowed her steps, her eyes narrowing as she took in the details. Who had hung these pieces? The framing was off, and the spacing between them looked... wrong. She felt a creeping sense of disquiet, like walking into a house that seemed familiar but wasn't right. Aurora's skin itched beneath her jacket, a tiny tremble setting itself up just below her shoulder.

A faint memory nagged at the back of her mind – an email from a gallery owner, maybe? Had she given permission for these pieces to be displayed? A cold sweat prickled at her hairline as she tried to recall the details. She felt exposed, like every private thought and emotion was being laid bare before a faceless crowd.

Aurora's eyes locked onto a single piece in particular – a vulnerable self-portrait, meant to remain personal and untouched by prying eyes. Whoever had hung it here had no right to do so, not without her permission. Her fists curled into tight buds at her sides as she weighed the options: speak out, or quietly disentangle herself from this situation before things escalated further.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Rachel clutched a steaming cup of coffee as she entered the gallery, its bright lights and loud chatter a jarring change from the peaceful morning she'd been enjoying. Her eyes began to scan the room, drinking in every detail – not just the art on display, but also her own hastily erected installation nearby.

A small table stood isolated near the far corner, cluttered with paint-splattered sketches and scraps of scribbled notes. Rachel's stomach twisted into knots as she took in its haphazard appearance. Why was it here? And who had brought it to the gallery in the first place? Her gaze lingered on a nearby flyer – an invitation to her own art show, but hosted by this verygallery?

A tiny tremble danced at the base of Rachel's spine. Had she accidentally RSVP'd for the wrong event? Was someone else trying to sabotage her chances with their own art, masquerading as hers in the process? As the room swirled and people milled about, she found herself shrinking into the background, hiding behind the safety net of coffee-cup-wielding anonymity. Her eyes fixed on a door that led out of this chaotic whirlwind – how to extract herself and restore some semblance of order?

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
She stared at it from across the room, as if it was an invader in her space. The photograph hung crookedly above the receptionist's desk – distorted and askew like a mocking mirror reflection. Every single thread of her being strained towards the exit door now, yearning for freedom from this forced confrontation.

At first glance, all seemed normal: a piece by some up-and-coming artist on loan to their studio space, maybe? Then she stumbled upon the fine print – those two tiny words that unraveled every strand of security surrounding her work. A creeping dread began to inscribe itself across her skin like cold, insistent finger-pressure.

Her internal alarm flashed red as reality crashed into what felt like a dissonant crescendo. She sprinted towards the exit without breaking stride or letting on – no questions asked, none required. All they needed were hastily scribbled lies in some bland contract or obscure waiver, to claim possession of her work over her screaming objections.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Jaxon sat hunched over his sketchbook, eyes scanning the row of exposed exhibits opposite him like a predator sensing weakness. Their art. His. All he'd ever created.

It hurt to see it splattered across an empty room without warning – not after years spent quietly producing those delicate drawings that wove themselves into the tapestry of people's lives in quiet whispers of beauty and awe. Something about this setting felt so... untrustworthy; a jumpy rabbit heart within his chest now, sensing every minute sound around him and jumping whenever anything out of place flanked him.

And then, like that unwelcome guest nobody'd invited – they had called it: an exhibit. With her pieces hung all over the room. Something within him seemed determined to stay hidden from a world in open mockery, no longer allowed the solace of quiet anonymity.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Lena slumped against the doorframe as she gazed out into the churning crowd – a sea that threatened to engulf every shred of her equilibrium like crashing waves. Flickers of panic flashed across her mind when something caught at the edge of perception, though it never stabilized long enough for Lena's thoughts to grasp onto.

Who'd decided this chaotic hodgepodge passed as an exhibit deserving attention? It felt like some twisted mirror where reflections danced and blurred until even identities themselves wavered – she stared into it in awe-horror. Every tiny step, however small her weight shifts might be within these concrete spaces, held back a tsunami of anguish.

A gentle sigh clawed at the surface as she took note that, amidst this tumult, lay familiar pieces – and maybe more to come? Lena let go slowly; something whispered it would be alright if she allowed herself to sink into the turbulent tides for just one moment longer...

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story: Alicia's feet felt like they'd been rooted to the floor as she stared at the large canvas dominating the gallery wall. Her latest series, "Ephemeral Whispers", had been her most intimate and vulnerable work yet. But how did it end up here? A patron in a sleek black suit approached her, beaming with pride. "Ah, Alicia, we were thinking of showcasing... ah, well, you see..." She interrupted him, her voice laced with incredulity, "This isn't even at its final iteration, I still have several pieces to complete. Where did these come from?"

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story: Lena's hands involuntarily rose to cover her mouth as she stepped into the exhibition space. Her artwork, splattered across a wall like bloodstains on a sidewalk, seemed to scream for help. Who had dared to do this? She mustered what little composure she could and pushed forward through the crowds of admiring onlookers. A curator caught her eye and, with an air of embarrassment, offered, "We thought it would be a great addition to our new collection." Lena's retort hovered like a hot breeze on the tip of her tongue.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story: Jamie blinked rapidly as he scanned the room for what felt like the hundredth time. One moment, his art was safely tucked away in his studio; the next, it was plastered across the city's most prominent gallery. An ex-girlfriend sauntered up to him now, a champagne flute hovering near her lips. "Wow, Jamie! You're really making waves!" Her tone sounded like a gong resonating off his eardrums – hollow and annoying.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission

"This isn't just about aesthetics! These pieces are still mine!" Someone else's hand hovered over his shoulder; it belonged to an acquaintance – no, more like a rival. "Ah, you see the bigger picture? It's fantastic exposure for all involved."

Zara slipped through the opening at the top of an imposing stone pedestal and took a seat on its narrow shelf, wrapping her arms around herself in a tight hold. A faint hum filled the air as people continued to admire the artworks hanging nearby – works that shouldn't be here. She bit down on the rim of her coffee cup, watching a middle-aged couple take turns posing before a canvas with her name attributed to it like a label on a designer shoe box.

Note: All these stories are distinct and independent of one another; no continuity is required.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Lena trudged through the gallery's crowded halls, her eyes scanning the walls for the one artwork that felt like a part of her. She had left it in storage, waiting to be rediscovered and recontextualized. But now, as she wove through the throng of admirers, she saw it – her latest piece – hung without permission or notification.

Her footsteps slowed, reluctance creeping into each step. She felt a flutter in her chest, like a bird struggling to free itself from its cage. The lights seemed too bright, and the chatter too loud; everything felt overwhelming and out of place.

People stopped before her work, tilting their heads one way and then another, but Lena's gaze remained fixed on something else: the framed white margin, stark against the vibrant colors that she had poured onto it. Her hand shook as if holding a cup too full of hot liquid.

"Doesn't it move you?" someone asked nearby, eyes bright with excitement.

A pause before she looked up at the speaker – no emotion revealed on her face. "It's just an arrangement of shapes," Lena said flatly, her voice betraying none of the turmoil inside. She turned and began to walk away from her art, leaving it behind in the unfamiliar environment.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
As he stepped into the gallery, Jasper's eyes widened, a mix of disorientation and unease settling heavy in his chest. Amidst all these people admiring every other piece except his own – he had submitted that work months ago; there was no way this could be right... but there it hung.

He walked stiffly across the tile floor, avoiding eye contact as others admired his creation without any recognition of its provenance. Jasper's hands felt empty and useless at his sides – a reminder of all the times they'd trembled with purpose when touching paint or carving stone blocks. Silence filled his head; not even background noise like murmurings seemed present.

He approached his piece, frozen as he surveyed it in this context. It hung unscathed but incongruous among so many other, seemingly better works. A hollowness crept upwards from his toes and spread outward to engulf much of him. 

A woman was gushing over another artist's painting two rooms down; nearby conversations grew in intensity without ever really connecting to the main subject – Jasper. The air around his art hung quietly, as if unwilling to startle him with sudden realization.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
She found a secluded nook amidst all those strangers admiring someone else's talents. She sat in slumped silence, elbows on knees. 

Her gaze drifted through tears that welled up and clung tight but refused to fall – though her whole face felt drenched by the weight of what she saw in public.

A hand shook like a single drop rippling across water while sketching the outline of a tiny flower; each stroke lost its meaning when forced out. Her pen trembled, unable to draw steady lines once they seemed to merge with anything resembling truth or accuracy – just as her artwork hung where no one took it seriously enough.

Why was this piece alone? Someone else's work next door glimmered golden-brown against shadows cast so that even light grew shadowy and difficult. Lena's breath shortened whenever thinking of all the people who would go on to live with an altered perspective, their attention wandering through someone else's colors instead of truly seeing.

The world beyond this confined air clung like a tight noose; she had almost forgotten it hung within reach. What difference would any action make? None at once – no, but soon maybe she must do something.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
His boots thudded quietly with each step across the floor as he made his way back to her work – already half-anticipating rejection and being asked (as always it seemed) to believe that it could coexist among more 'impor-tant' pieces of art. Each pace a slow, heavy beat echoed back from somewhere deeper than where it originated.

A sense of disorientation crept over him as he stopped before his creation – suspended between disbelief at how easily others accepted, praised and hung it up alongside others without so much as discussing any doubts or controversies associated with its provenance – or maybe because none existed? He folded arms across chest but said nothing; voice snagged a moment below in dry gulleys between laryngeal cartilage.

People started to take their leave – they'd get home soon and sleep off fatigue while he lay awake questioning this turn-of-events. Silence was what came next, and Jasper stood quietly amidst the hush until one last person turned away.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
From afar, she watched as strangers praised her best pieces without actually seeing them at all. All those people thronging around someone else's mediocre work and talking loudly about its significance seemed to blur into a distant hum – background static that failed even to reach the surface level of awareness. She let fingers brush against legs beneath an oversized skirt.

A hesitant approach to that spot where hers hung isolated amidst the crowded exhibition space... felt like stepping over a ledge, unsure if it contained air and support or a hollow drop into something else entirely unknown. Lena couldn't shake off this sinking feeling as if she'd crossed boundaries nobody meant for her to cross – at least not yet; but maybe they'd be glad once that happened too.

The gentle lighthouse beam of evening sunlight streaming through gallery windows helped nothing – seemed cold instead of welcoming, and somehow just out of reach.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Lena stormed into the gallery, her eyes scanning the crowded room with a mix of anger and betrayal. She felt a familiar knot forming in her stomach as she spotted her latest series on display without her permission. The bright lights and chatter were like nails on a chalkboard to her sensitive ears.

She pushed through the crowd, her elbows sharp as she forced people out of her way. "Excuse me," she snapped, not looking up from her gaze fixed on the offending artwork. A nearby patron hesitated before yielding, but Lena didn't slow down until she reached the small talkative curator by the corner.

"Where's the explanation?" she demanded, her voice low and even but laced with a thinly veiled threat.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Ricardo stood in front of his own painting, hands clenched into fists as he gazed at it with a feeling akin to being punched in the gut. The vibrant colors that had once brought him such joy now struck him with a dull ache. Why was this piece here? Hadn't they explicitly stated that none of their work would be shared outside the studio?

He felt like running, but his feet seemed rooted to the spot as he forced himself to examine every detail on display. Even the title – an inside joke between him and his best friend – had been altered without anyone's knowledge or consent.

"How could you do this?" Ricardo muttered under his breath, eyes scanning the room for some sign of responsibility, but finding none.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Miranda stared at her artwork spread across a white backdrop like a thief staring down the barrel of a metaphorical gun. It was as if someone had taken her very soul – those late nights spent pouring her heart into creation – and put it out there, hanging for anyone to touch, anyone to judge.

Her breath caught in a sharp inhale as she spotted someone laughing at her piece from across the room. Not just any laughter, but that rich, full-bodied chuckle one might find in a champagne toast or at a stand-up comedy night. Her gaze narrowed, freezing in place like ice. If she let him continue, it'd start to feel more than intrusive – it'd become sacrilegious.

Miranda turned on her heel and moved with stealth towards the corner of the room where security would be, a plan beginning to form behind her gritted teeth.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Celine stood frozen near the entrance, trying not to notice the murmurs as they passed around whispers of "that artist" in front of her piece. They seemed to think it was just some passing fascination – something a struggling student might churn out on a Tuesday morning. It killed her: every fiber in her being begged her to speak up, show them what made this work more than the sum of its mundane canvas and paint.

Her eyes flashed towards the artist in question (some new import from Berlin), but Celine wasn't sure if she was disappointed by their obvious non-interest or relieved – after all, perhaps a disconnection would be healthy? The gallery itself glowed with an overly polished charm. As a whole, everything here radiated pretentiousness to her sensitive psyche.

A small crowd nearby caught sight of Celine watching the display and, instinctively, they turned towards her. The artist's eyes slid over like she didn't exist – except she was very much there, a silent, festering wound waiting for someone to see its anguish.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Dr. Vasquez gazed at his work through a blur of anger, as if all the blood in his body had rushed to one place – a pressure cooker in danger of explosion. For weeks now he'd been hearing buzz about this gallery's 'groundbreaking' feature: "uncommissioned pieces from various artists", and yet none had approached him with any sort of genuine interest in sharing his art.

It made his gut clench whenever he thought that maybe people saw these artworks not as things created with intention, sweat, and tears – but mere accessories, shiny trinkets to be bought and discarded. If only the viewers knew what truly went into every line, each curve of paint on surface... perhaps they'd see it, really see it.

"Stop pretending," he muttered to nobody in particular, trying to make a subtle turn towards the exit. Some people might have taken offense, but Dr. Vasquez had no desire for that; all he wanted was distance – from judgmental faces and patronizing smiles, or at least some sort of apology...

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Emily stormed into the gallery, her eyes scanning the crowded room for one person. She spotted him across the way, sipping champagne and smiling for all the wrong reasons. Emily's jaw clamped shut as she watched David laugh with a patron who was holding up Emily's latest piece. The sculpture, called "Echoes of Silence," looked lost behind layers of plexiglass. She had poured her heart into it, and this...this travesty couldn't have been further from what she intended.

The glass wall reflected the chaos in her mind: shattered remains of a thought once held dear. Emily's face was a mask now, but inside, she felt like she was disintegrating into tiny shards.

David spotted her storming towards him and raised an eyebrow. "A bit too enthusiastic about your own work, don't you think?" he said with a smirk, patting Emma (she corrected herself mentally).

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
I watched as my paintings were paraded around like so many cheap trinkets. The gallery owner was beaming, but I couldn't match his enthusiasm. My skin crawled at the sight of those people handling my work without permission. One man even lit a cigar next to "Whispers" – who did he think I was painting for? Himself? I felt like I'd been punched in the gut.

What was he even thinking? Did he hate me? Or was this just some twisted game?

Someone nudged my arm, holding out a glass of champagne. I shook it off, and it clattered against the floor.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Kato's eyes roved the crowded room like a trapped predator. Some fool's words spilled over into his mind – something about 'new and avant-garde'. His gut churned.

People laughed around him as they walked past "Rainfall" propped up on an easel. Kato's fingers flexed into fists, involuntarily digging into the backrest of the chair he sat behind the wall display table.

What a travesty...it was still in its primordial state! They should see it done with fire and passion – done as I meant!

I took a deep breath; no one here really understood. The art critics? No, they didn't either.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
Pilar's voice rose above the hum of chatter like a protest sign. She'd arrived early, catching David mid-wait to charm her into smiling about this monstrosity he'd turned my art room into.

"David," she said sharply, shaking off his arm, as if it clung there like the layers of gauze now adorning "Silence". "Have you seen what's being exhibited here?"

The patrons around us grew quieter, curiosity piqued. Some murmured – did they not even recognize this abomination was mine? I'd poured a life into it.

"I...uh," David stammered with an inane expression.

topic: An artist's work is displayed without their permission
story:
It wasn't right. Not at all. My work: broken up and rearranged like some puzzle to be solved by outsiders' eyes alone. The owner didn't even bother hiding behind 'experts'; his gleeful attitude reeked of opportunism.

Savannah stood on the edge, feeling disconnected from it all – a fragile, crumbling thing exposed in front of all these people. Something inside was beginning to burn.

How could they know what I saw? What I intended for her gaze only? It didn't belong here like this...
